patch_description: Building on the best-scoring prior variant (2 distinct circuit parameters: a global `theta_ry` local-rotation angle and a global `theta_z` angle shared by both the RZ layer and all CRZ entanglers across three connectivity shells — nearest-neighbor, skip, and antipodal), this version follows the recommended zero-parameter-growth enrichment: after every CRZ edge in all three shells, a matching CRX gate on the SAME wire pair is inserted, reusing the identical `theta_z` parameter (no new param names introduced). This turns each entangling edge from a single Z-Z-type coupling into a combined Z-Z + X-mediated coupling (non-commuting rotation axes), giving the ansatz a richer, less commutative entangling structure without touching the trainable parameter count (still 2 distinct circuit params, 4 total with gain/bias). The intuition: since parameter economy is rewarded at every step and the current search plateaued at 4 distinct params, forcing more expressive multi-axis entanglement while holding parameter count fixed is the most direct way to raise the worst-group margin (better boundary shaping) and to shrink the train/validation/test gap, since the extra structure comes from architecture, not from more free parameters that could overfit the tiny training set.
